comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

comments.body:
> We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's

Are they just lacking reviews in the mailing list? Or are there other concerns?

I understand we also need an apparmor patch for libvirt, and a versioned breaks in qemu to force the upgrade of libvirt if it's installed, right?

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
Apologies for the delay on getting this updated. The two follow-up patches were merged upstream on Monday. I've included updated information for those, and a commit adding the Breaks for libvirt.

@hector I used `git-ubuntu queue sync` to base these patches on ubuntu8.20 in unapproved; please let me know if any changes here would make your life easier :)

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…to 64. This could produce a performance regression for some users, as the performance bottleneck of this cap was significant enoug…" (whershberger)

The libvirt AppArmor change (needed so QEMU can read /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count) is tracked in a separate bug (2170732), not as a libvirt task on this bug. Without it, AppArmor-confined VMs lose the pool cap and the fix is ineffective. The libvirt update must be released, and its SRU coordinated, before or with the qemu update.

The versioned Breaks on libvirt, added in the merge proposal, can only be satisfied if the fixed libvirt version is already available in the same pocket. The upload ordering and dependency are not confirmed, so the qemu upload could be uninstallable or held back.

The two follow-up fixes (the max_map_count parsing fix and the conservative default cap) were only merged upstream recently. The bug description's 'Source patches' list and 'Where problems could occur' text still treat them as external or unapplied. The description should list these commits explicitly and say that the upload includes them.

The bug now targets newer supported releases, but the Impact text still says the issue only affects 24.04. Those releases need the fix in the development release first, and the description should be made consistent with the series being targeted.

The test plan does not verify that the pool cap works when AppArmor is active and the fixed libvirt is installed. It also gives no before/after performance regression results yet, even though the plan itself says the new lock in coroutine_pool_get and the hard pool cap could cause regressions.
